No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Air Force Explores Satellite Communications, Tracking Technology For Aircraft Upgrade by Yusuf Babalola 5 seconds ago in Business Share on WhatsApp Share on Facebook Share on X Telegram The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has held strategic discussions with Fohat Solutions Limited and its Canadian technology partner, SKYTRAC Systems Ltd., on plans to explore satellite communications, aircraft tracking and other advanced aerospace technologies to modernise its air assets and strengthen operational capabilities.
The proposed collaboration is expected to introduce advanced aviation technologies into Nigeria’s military aviation infrastructure, enhance mission effectiveness and improve the operational readiness of the Air Force.
The discussions were held during the recently concluded Africa International Defence Exhibition (AFRIDEX 2026) in Lagos.
The meeting was facilitated by the Canadian Trade Commissioner Service and brought together senior representatives of the Nigerian Air Force, Fohat Solutions and SKYTRAC.
Representing the Chief of the Air Staff, Air Vice Marshal Bamidele, the Director of Air Operations welcomed the proposed collaboration and expressed the Nigerian Air Force’s willingness to explore SKYTRAC’s solutions in support of aircraft modernisation and operational enhancement.
The discussions focused on potential upgrades involving satellite-enabled avionics, secure airborne communications, real-time aircraft tracking, flight data monitoring and advanced mission-support technologies.
Speaking at the meeting, James Kim, Head of Office and Senior Trade Commissioner, representing the Canadian Trade Commissioner Service, highlighted growing opportunities for technological cooperation between Nigeria and Canada
He emphasised the importance of connecting Canadian technological innovation with Nigeria’s defence modernisation objectives through partnerships that promote knowledge exchange and industrial cooperation.
SKYTRAC’s Director of Business Development, Jeff Sherwood, explained how the company’s aviation connectivity technologies could improve situational awareness, strengthen communications between aircraft and ground command
centres, and enhance the coordination of complex military missions.
He also highlighted opportunities to upgrade existing aircraft with advanced systems to improve their operational capabilities.
Headquartered in Canada, SKYTRAC provides satellite communications, intelligent aircraft connectivity and mission-critical aerospace solutions to military, government and commercial aviation operators.
The proposed partnership could support surveillance, reconnaissance, operational readiness and aviation safety, while creating opportunities for technical training and the development of local expertise.
Chief Executive Officer of Fohat Solutions Limited, Alfred Idiodi, reaffirmed the company’s commitment to advancing Nigeria’s defence and aviation capabilities through the deployment of world-class technology, technology transfer and indigenous capacity development.
“Our partnership with SKYTRAC goes beyond technology deployment. We aim to facilitate specialised training and knowledge transfer for Nigerian Air Force personnel, empowering them to operate and sustain advanced aviation systems while strengthening operational readiness, mission effectiveness and long-term technological self-reliance,” Idiodi stated.
The engagement is expected to pave the way for further technical consultations as the parties explore areas of collaboration to strengthen Nigeria’s air power, modernise existing aircraft and improve the country’s long-term military aviation capabilities.
